title: Eleven Entries and One Cup
subtitle: 竞技体育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）
meta: 主题语境：竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）　|　核心词汇：contest　|　正文 330 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 contest 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 my brother ① entered a contest with eleven entries and one cup, and he said the entering was the whole of the training. The ② contest, meaning the event and not the cup, took one afternoon and stayed that size; contest, he said, is the only thing in a field that is judged by how many stay to the end.

Every ③ contest in that village had the same judge, and the ④ contest at the end, meaning the one he kept for the harvest and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever argued about twice. Contest, my mother said, is nine parts judging and one part somebody willing to accept it; my brother said the accepting is the part that fills the afternoon.

My grandfather meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the contest was the whole of the meeting, meaning the struggle and not the event. The ⑥ contest, meaning the struggle and not any of that, is the only thing in a meeting that everybody feels and nobody enters; contest, he said, is either something you enter or the only word that means both an event and a struggle. She said the struggle is the part they remember.

By 1969 the ⑦ contest had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the judge. The ⑧ contest of the whole thing, my brother wrote in August, was one field and thirty years of accepting; contest, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to accept. He said the accepting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ contest I remember is the one at the end, which was held in 1975 and is still described as the fullest in the county. A ⑩ contest, my mother said in 1977, is the only thing that improves by being argued about; every contest, she said, is a struggle that has agreed to look like an event. She said the struggle was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 比赛（指那场赛事本身，与那只奖杯相对）
C. 固定搭配：enter a contest 参加比赛
D. n. 比赛（指那个村子里每一届）
E. n. 比赛（指末尾那一届）
F. n. 争夺；角逐（抽象：那场较劲）
G. n. 比赛（指节目单里提到的那一届）
H. n. 竞赛；较量（抽象总称）

items.q: entered a contest with eleven entries and one cup
The contest, meaning the event and not the cup
the contest was the whole of the meeting
the contest had become a line in a programme
The contest of the whole thing
A contest, my mother said in 1977

answers.why: enter a contest 意为“参加比赛”，1961 年哥哥参加了一场有十一人报名、只设一只奖杯的比赛。
contest 意为“比赛”，指那场赛事本身而不是那只奖杯，它占了一个下午。
contest 指那个村子里每一届比赛，每一届都是同一个裁判。
contest 指末尾那一届（他留给丰收节的那届），是唯一有人争论过两次的。
contest 意为“争夺、角逐”，祖父说那场较劲就是那次会议的全部，指的是较劲而不是那场比赛。
contest 为抽象用法，指那场较劲而不是那场比赛，是会议里人人都感觉到、却无人报名参加的东西。
contest 意为“比赛”，指节目单里提到的那一届，到 1969 年这场比赛成了节目单里的一行。
contest 意为“竞赛、较量”，哥哥八月写道，整件事的较量是一片场地三十年的接受结果。
contest 意为“比赛”，我记得的是末尾那一届，1975 年举办，至今仍被说成全县参赛人数最多的。
contest 为抽象总称，母亲说一场比赛是唯一会因为被争论而变好的东西。
